doc.title: Joseph Rene and Edna Kelly Interview, 1969-12-15

chapter: Joe Rene: Lewis, the Rena band and New Orleans
title: Spelling of the Rene/Rena name
summary: Rene explains why he spells the name differently from his brother, as a Creole backward habit.

story.theme_name: How I got my name: nicknames and band monikers
story.community_name: How I got my name: nicknames and band names

blocks.x: Yeah. Now you pronounce your name Rene, don't you? Rene Everson. Your brother, you spell it R-E-N-A. Well, now, you see, we used to spell it R-E-N-A. Yes.

But one time come, I had to have my voice that people would find it was R-E-N-E. Instead of Rene, instead of E, instead of A, it's E. See, you know how Creole people, always used things backwards. Now that, he had the sound of E, you see, and we used to go by that.

But it was R-E-N-E. That was quite serious. How did your brother pronounce it? Did you pronounce it Rene the same? Yeah, that's all right. Now, how did you actually, can you remember how you actually first met George when you were saying, like up there on Governor Nicholson? On Governor Nicholson? Yeah, I mean, I was passing. Remember, I tell you that, I was passing.
